page: Amazon Web Services r5a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is built on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It features 128 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage, requiring reliance on remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data, and features a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the system delivers balanced throughput for multithreaded and memory-bound operations, achieved alongside moderate compute intensity. In PassMark testing, the instance posted an overall CPU score of 12,528.87 and a memory score of 1,973.90, alongside 3,728.78 on database operations. Redis SET operations reached 9.96 million operations per second, reflecting solid suitability for in-memory key-value processing. Conversely, single-thread CPU performance is limited, registering a Geekbench single-core score of 727.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 591.29. Uncached memory throughput also shows constraints, with large-block read bandwidth measuring 27.56 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaching 13.24 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the r5a.4xlarge lies in its reliance on first-generation AMD EPYC architecture, which exhibits lower per-core compute efficiency and unaccelerated memory write speeds relative to newer memory-intensive offerings. However, it provides favorable cost efficiency for memory footprint capacity, supplying 128 GB of RAM without demanding excessive compute licensing overhead. The configuration is best aligned with in-memory caching systems such as Redis, relational databases, data extraction pipelines, and general enterprise applications with high memory footprints and moderate CPU compute demands.
description: Amazon Web Services r5a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance utilizing an AMD EPYC 7571 processor at 2.5 GHz with Nitro hypervisor management. The configuration delivers 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and 128 GB of DDR4 system memory, achieving an 8.0 GB per vCPU distribution. Network performance is anchored by a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while persistent storage must be attached externally as no local storage is bundled. Benchmark results show average multi-core processing with a PassMark CPU score of 12,528.87 and Redis performance at 9.96 million operations per second, though single-core execution and uncached memory write bandwidth rank in lower tiers. Delivering cost-effective memory capacity, the instance is targeted at in-memory caching, mid-tier database hosting, and memory-bound operational workloads requiring high RAM density over raw single-thread speed.
